title: RAG's Hidden Flaw: No Metadata

steps.status: app sends query vector to DB
llm generates bad answer from bad contex
app extracts metadata filters from query
filter passes query & metadata to DB
app sends precise context to llm

caption: Your RAG retrieves garbage. Here's why.When building RAG, simply relying on vector similarity can lead to irrelevant context. Here's what actually happens:1. USER: You ask a question, perhaps specifying details like a date or project name.2. RAG APP: Your application converts your query into a vector for similarity search.3. VECTOR DB: The vector database returns documents that are semantically similar but might ignore crucial filtering criteria like date ranges or specific categories.4. LLM: The LLM receives this potentially irrelevant context.5. RAG APP: The application presents a poor or hallucinated answer, because the context was not precise.6. RAG APP (with filter): Your application *also* extracts specific metadata filters (e.g., `date > '2023-01-01'`, `project_id = 'XYZ'`) from your query.7. METADATA FILTER: Before vector search, a metadata filter component (often built into the vector DB itself) narrows down the search space to only documents matching these criteria.8. VECTOR DB (filtered): The vector database now performs similarity search *only* on the pre-filtered set of documents, ensuring relevance.9. RAG APP (relevant): The application receives a highly relevant and precise set of documents.10. LLM (accurate): The LLM generates a much more accurate and grounded response.Effective metadata filtering is a critical, often overlooked, component of a robust RAG system, ensuring your LLM gets the *right* context, not just *any* context.Precision in retrieval isn't magic; it's about smart filtering.📌 Save this so you don't build bad RAG.🔁 Send it to someone struggling with RAG quality.Written by Kai.Follow @byteflowlabs for AI systems, no hype.
takeaway: Precision in retrieval isn't magic; it's about smart filtering.
